title: cost-optimization: autotune defaults for batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Priya Kapoor
description: Summary: Add an end-to-end autotune flow that sets improved defaults for batching and KV-prefix caching, introduces model quantization profile recommendations, and surfaces unit-economics (UEcon) metrics in the Console and CLI. Motivation: customers pay for per-token inference; many workloads are suboptimal w.r.t batching and cache settings and run on suboptimal quantization profiles. We need a safer, automated defaults path that improves median token cost without regressing tail latency or quality. This PR wires the autotune controller, runtime heuristics, quant-profile selector, and UEcon tooling. What this PR contains (one continuous description): Implements an autotune controller that collects per-route telemetry (median/95p latency, batch sizes, cache hit rates, tokens per request) and computes recommended defaults for continuous_batching.window_ms and kv_cache.prefix_size. Adds quantization profile scoring that evaluates candidate quant levels (fp16, int8, q4f, q4h) against a lightweight quality regression test harness (prompt set + BLEU/embedding similarity threshold). Introduces UEcon tooling: a CI job that computes expected cost delta and a Console dashboard panel showing estimated unit-cost, expected savings, and risk score for applying the recommendation. Adds API flags to opt into automatic rollouts (canary percentage, cooldown windows). Includes migration script to backfill recommended defaults for existing model routes. Adds docs and telemetry dashboards. Checklist: - [x] runtime heuristics and gating - [x] autotune controller and API - [x] quantization profile selector + regression harness - [x] UEcon dashboard + CLI tooling - [x] e2e tests + unit tests - [x] docs and release notes Testing and safety: Recommendations are generated but not applied by default. The rollout path uses a canary percentage + automatic rollback when 95p latency increases > 10% or quality drop > configured threshold. We ran a 2-week internal canary across 5 routes (chat summarization, search rerank, code completion, embeddings) showing median token-cost reduction of 18% (range 8%-32%) with no quality regressions above thresholds. See results/benchmarks in the commits section. Rollout plan: opt-in for now; gradual enable via opt-in flag in Console and customer API; full enable behind account-level feature flag after 6 weeks of extended monitoring.
